title: Teen-Led Pantry de la Comunidad Brings Two New Pantries to Independence Hills Park
excerpt: Pantry de la Comunidad, a nonprofit led by Laredo high school students, is adding two new pantries — one for food, one for hygiene items — at Independence Hills Park in District I.
content:
A teen-founded Laredo nonprofit is growing again. Pantry de la Comunidad is bringing two new community pantries to Independence Hills Park — one stocked with food and one with hygiene products — after collecting about 150 food items to date.

District I Council Member Gilbert Gonzalez announced the new pantries on November 13 at Independence Hills Park, in the 3100 block of Independence Hills, according to the Laredo Morning Times. The pantries will be built by the Bertina family and installed when the weather cools, followed by a ribbon-cutting ceremony.

The nonprofit is led by high school students Katalina Chapa and Danna Gaitan. Its first pantry was built in July 2024 on the 1800 block of San Dario Avenue, sponsored by the Gaitan family. Other pantries stand on the 1500 block of Hillside Road and the 800 block of Los Ebanos Drive.

Residents can donate nonperishable food, clothing and hygiene products, or reach the group on Instagram, Facebook and TikTok at @pantrydelacomunidad.

Gonzalez said District I has one of the city’s highest food-insecurity rates. The council has allocated $75,000 to revamp Independence Hills Park, including bathrooms, electrical work, fencing, parking and repairs to play equipment.

Chapa said the pantries are meant to give people hope, and the group hopes to expand to every district in the city.
